# Introduction

The transduced cells carry a lentiviral cassette, `SFFV → mCherry → P2A → DRE`, whose transcript runs
on through WPRE and the 3′ LTR to a polyadenylation site in the LTR's R region. P2A means mCherry and
DRE are translated as separate proteins from a **single mRNA**, so the three features annotated on the
cassette are three windows onto one molecule, not three genes.

| Feature | Position on the contig | Distance from the polyA site |
|---------|------------------------|------------------------------|
| `mCherry` | 1–708 | ~2,900 bases |
| `DRE` | 781–1830 | ~1,360 bases |
| `WPRE-LTR` | 1939–3236 | 0–1,300 bases |

That last column is what this report is about. 10x 3′ chemistry attaches the cell barcode and UMI at
the polyA tail during reverse transcription, and the final PCR amplifies only the fragment still
carrying that barcode — so reads fall within roughly 300–600 bases of the tail. A feature's detection
rate is therefore set as much by its position as by how much transcript the cell holds.

These cells also come with an **independent ground truth**: they were FACS-sorted on mCherry protein
before sequencing, and the sort fraction is recorded in `sample.name.long`. That lets us ask not just
which feature detects most, but which detections are right.

```{r setup}
library(Seurat)
library(targets)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)
library(DT)
library(Matrix)
source(file.path("src/R/scrna-seq_utilities.R"))

#' Pull the Transgene counts, sort label and UMAP coordinates out of a processed object.
#' Returns a small tibble so the Seurat objects need not be held in memory together.
transgene_table <- function(srt) {
  tg  <- Seurat::GetAssayData(srt, assay = "Transgene", layer = "counts")
  emb <- Seurat::Embeddings(srt, "umap.nn")
  tibble::tibble(
    cell        = colnames(srt),
    tube        = srt$tube,
    sample      = srt$sample.name.long,
    compartment = srt$compartment,
    pass_cell   = srt$pass_cell,
    UMAP_1      = emb[, 1],
    UMAP_2      = emb[, 2]
  ) %>%
    dplyr::bind_cols(as.data.frame(as.matrix(Matrix::t(tg)), check.names = FALSE))
}

hsc <- transgene_table(tar_read(mpn_raw_processed_hsc)); gc()
mnc <- transgene_table(tar_read(mpn_raw_processed_mnc)); gc()

features <- c("mCherry", "DRE", "WPRE-LTR")

cells <- dplyr::bind_rows(hsc, mnc) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    # The sort fraction, from the suffix the sample sheet carries
    sorted = dplyr::case_when(
      grepl("_positive$", sample)  ~ "FACS mCherry+",
      grepl("_negative$", sample)  ~ "FACS mCherry−",
      grepl("wildtype",   sample)  ~ "wild-type (no vector)"
    ),
    sorted = factor(sorted, levels = c("FACS mCherry+", "FACS mCherry−",
                                       "wild-type (no vector)"))
  )
rm(hsc, mnc); gc()
```

## What the sort labels are

```{r truth-table}
cells %>%
  dplyr::count(tube, compartment, sample, sorted, name = "cells") %>%
  dplyr::arrange(tube) %>%
  DT::datatable(rownames = FALSE, options = list(dom = "t", pageLength = 10))
```

Three groups matter, and they are not interchangeable:

- **wild-type** tubes never saw the vector, so any signal there is assay error — ambient transcript
  or mismapping. These give the false-positive floor.
- **FACS mCherry+** cells carry the vector *and* express mCherry protein above the sort gate.
- **FACS mCherry−** cells failed that gate. That is a statement about protein, not about DNA or RNA,
  which turns out to matter a great deal.


# Comparing the three features

```{r long-form}
long <- cells %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(dplyr::all_of(features), names_to = "feature", values_to = "umi") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(feature = factor(feature, levels = features))

per_sample <- long %>%
  dplyr::group_by(tube, compartment, sorted, feature) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(cells = dplyr::n(),
                   pos   = sum(umi > 0),
                   pct   = 100 * pos / cells,
                   mean_umi_pos = ifelse(pos > 0, sum(umi) / pos, NA_real_),
                   .groups = "drop")
```

```{r detection-plot, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 4.5}
ggplot(per_sample, aes(tube, pct, fill = feature)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.75) +
  facet_grid(~ sorted, scales = "free_x", space = "free_x") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "cells with ≥1 UMI (%)", fill = NULL,
       title = "Detection by feature, tube and sort fraction") +
  theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "top",
                     axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

```{r detection-table}
per_sample %>%
  dplyr::mutate(label = sprintf("%d (%.2f%%)", pos, pct)) %>%
  dplyr::select(tube, sorted, cells, feature, label) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = feature, values_from = label) %>%
  DT::datatable(rownames = FALSE, options = list(dom = "t", pageLength = 10))
```

## mCherry against DRE

Both sit on the same mRNA, so in a cell expressing the cassette either could in principle be
detected. They differ only in distance from the polyA site — DRE is about 1.5 kb closer.

```{r mcherry-vs-dre}
cells %>%
  dplyr::group_by(tube, sorted) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    `mCherry only` = sum(mCherry > 0 & DRE == 0),
    `DRE only`     = sum(mCherry == 0 & DRE > 0),
    both           = sum(mCherry > 0 & DRE > 0),
    `DRE / mCherry rate` = round(sum(DRE > 0) / pmax(1, sum(mCherry > 0)), 2),
    `expected if independent` = round(sum(mCherry > 0) * sum(DRE > 0) / dplyr::n()),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  DT::datatable(rownames = FALSE, options = list(dom = "t", pageLength = 10))
```

DRE is detected in more cells than mCherry, as its position predicts. But the two sets overlap far
less than one might expect of a single transcript: a large share of mCherry-positive cells are
DRE-negative and vice versa, and the "both" count, while above the figure expected if the two were
sampled independently, is nowhere near nesting.

That is informative rather than contradictory. At one or two UMIs per cell, each feature is a
near-independent Bernoulli draw from the same small pool of molecules — detecting one tells you
little about whether the other was also captured. Poor overlap is what shallow sampling of a shared
transcript looks like, and it is a reason not to treat "mCherry⁻ but DRE⁺" as biologically
meaningful.

## Both against WPRE-LTR

```{r vs-wpre}
cells %>%
  dplyr::group_by(tube, sorted) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    `WPRE-LTR+`                   = sum(`WPRE-LTR` > 0),
    `mCherry+ and WPRE-LTR+`      = sum(mCherry > 0 & `WPRE-LTR` > 0),
    `mCherry+ but WPRE-LTR−` = sum(mCherry > 0 & `WPRE-LTR` == 0),
    `DRE+ but WPRE-LTR−`     = sum(DRE > 0 & `WPRE-LTR` == 0),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  DT::datatable(rownames = FALSE, options = list(dom = "t", pageLength = 10),
                caption = "Cells positive for a coding feature are almost always WPRE-LTR positive too")
```

The nesting is near-complete: a cell positive for mCherry or DRE is almost always positive for
`WPRE-LTR`, while the reverse fails often. The three features behave as one measurement observed with
three different sensitivities, ordered exactly by distance from the polyA site.

## Distribution of each reporter across samples

Most cells have no reporter UMI at all, so a violin over all cells collapses onto zero. The violins
below show how many UMIs a cell carries **where the reporter is detected**; the label above each is
the share of the sample's cells that have it (and how many cells that is).

```{r sample-labels}
# One tube per sample: label samples by compartment and sort fraction
sort_short <- c("FACS mCherry+" = "mCh+", "FACS mCherry−" = "mCh−", "wild-type (no vector)" = "WT")
long <- long %>%
  dplyr::mutate(sample_label = factor(paste(compartment, sort_short[as.character(sorted)]),
                                      levels = as.vector(outer(c("HSC", "MNC"),
                                                               c("WT", "mCh−", "mCh+"), paste))))
cells <- cells %>%
  dplyr::mutate(sample_label = factor(paste(compartment, sort_short[as.character(sorted)]),
                                      levels = levels(long$sample_label)))
```

```{r violin-per-sample, fig.width = 11, fig.height = 4.5}
detected_lab <- long %>%
  dplyr::group_by(feature, sample_label) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(label = sprintf("%.1f%%\n(%d)", 100 * mean(umi > 0), sum(umi > 0)),
                   .groups = "drop")

# A violin needs enough cells to mean anything: below 20 positive cells, show the cells themselves
min_violin <- 20
pos <- long %>%
  dplyr::filter(umi > 0) %>%
  dplyr::add_count(feature, sample_label, name = "n_pos")

ggplot(pos, aes(sample_label, umi, fill = feature)) +
  geom_violin(data = ~ dplyr::filter(.x, n_pos >= min_violin),
              scale = "width", alpha = 0.6, colour = NA) +
  geom_boxplot(data = ~ dplyr::filter(.x, n_pos >= min_violin),
               width = 0.15, outlier.shape = NA, fill = "white") +
  geom_jitter(data = ~ dplyr::filter(.x, n_pos < min_violin), aes(colour = feature),
              width = 0.15, height = 0.03, size = 1) +
  geom_text(data = detected_lab, aes(sample_label, Inf, label = label),
            vjust = 1.2, size = 2.8, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~ feature, nrow = 1) +
  scale_x_discrete(limits = levels(long$sample_label)) +   # layers hold different samples: keep the order
  scale_y_log10(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.35))) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "UMIs per positive cell (log scale)",
       title = "Reporter depth in positive cells, per sample",
       subtitle = sprintf("label: %% of the sample's cells with ≥1 UMI (number of cells); points where fewer than %d cells", min_violin)) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "none", axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

## Pairwise comparisons between reporters

Each pair of reporters, sample by sample. Since the three are windows on one transcript, a cell with
deep expression should show all of them; at shallow depth each is captured more or less on its own.

```{r pairs-long}
pairs <- list(c("mCherry", "DRE"), c("mCherry", "WPRE-LTR"), c("DRE", "WPRE-LTR"))

pair_df <- lapply(pairs, function(p) {
  cells %>%
    dplyr::transmute(sample_label, pair = paste(p[1], "vs", p[2]),
                     a = .data[[p[1]]], b = .data[[p[2]]])
}) %>%
  dplyr::bind_rows() %>%
  dplyr::mutate(pair = factor(pair, levels = sapply(pairs, paste, collapse = " vs ")))
```

```{r pairs-scatter, fig.width = 12, fig.height = 7}
# Counts are small integers: plot how many cells sit at each (a, b) combination
pair_df %>%
  dplyr::filter(a > 0 | b > 0) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(a = pmin(a, 10), b = pmin(b, 10)) %>%
  dplyr::count(pair, sample_label, a, b, name = "cells") %>%
  ggplot(aes(a, b, size = cells, colour = log10(cells))) +
  geom_point() +
  facet_grid(pair ~ sample_label) +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 6) +
  scale_colour_viridis_c(guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(0, 5, 10), labels = c("0", "5", "≥10")) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = c(0, 5, 10), labels = c("0", "5", "≥10")) +
  labs(x = "UMIs of the first reporter (capped at 10)",
       y = "UMIs of the second reporter (capped at 10)",
       title = "UMIs of each reporter pair, per sample (cells with either reporter)") +
  theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "right")
```

```{r pairs-table}
pair_stats <- pair_df %>%
  dplyr::group_by(pair, sample_label) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    cells       = dplyr::n(),
    `first+`    = sum(a > 0),
    `second+`   = sum(b > 0),
    both        = sum(a > 0 & b > 0),
    jaccard     = both / pmax(1, sum(a > 0 | b > 0)),
    `P(second+ | first+)` = both / pmax(1, `first+`),
    `P(first+ | second+)` = both / pmax(1, `second+`),
    # rank correlation among cells carrying either reporter (zeros everywhere else would dominate)
    spearman    = if (sum(a > 0 | b > 0) >= 10)
                    suppressWarnings(cor(a[a > 0 | b > 0], b[a > 0 | b > 0], method = "spearman"))
                  else NA_real_,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

pair_stats %>%
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(c(jaccard, `P(second+ | first+)`, `P(first+ | second+)`, spearman),
                              ~ round(.x, 3))) %>%
  DT::datatable(rownames = FALSE, filter = "top",
                options = list(pageLength = 18, dom = "tip"),
                caption = "Co-detection per reporter pair and sample")
```

```{r pairs-conditional, fig.width = 11, fig.height = 4}
# A rate from a handful of cells is noise: leave out those conditioned on fewer than 20 cells
min_cond <- 20
pair_stats %>%
  dplyr::mutate(`P(second+ | first+)` = ifelse(`first+`  >= min_cond, `P(second+ | first+)`, NA),
                `P(first+ | second+)` = ifelse(`second+` >= min_cond, `P(first+ | second+)`, NA)) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(`P(second+ | first+)`, `P(first+ | second+)`),
                      names_to = "direction", values_to = "p") %>%
  ggplot(aes(sample_label, p, fill = direction)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.75) +
  facet_wrap(~ pair, nrow = 1) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "co-detection", fill = NULL,
       title = "How often one reporter is detected where the other is",
       subtitle = paste0("e.g. for mCherry vs WPRE-LTR, P(second+ | first+) = share of mCherry+ cells that are WPRE-LTR+;\n",
                         "no bar: fewer than ", min_cond, " cells to condition on (counts in the table above)")) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "top", axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

Read the conditional rates against the positions on the transcript: detection of the reporter
nearer the polyA site (`WPRE-LTR`, then `DRE`) given the farther one should be high in every sample
that has real expression, while the reverse stays low. In the wild-type samples, where every count is
assay error, the pairs should show no co-detection beyond chance.

```{r umi-depth, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 4}
long %>%
  dplyr::filter(umi > 0, sorted %in% c("FACS mCherry+", "FACS mCherry−")) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(umi_capped = pmin(umi, 10)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(factor(umi_capped), fill = feature)) +
  geom_bar(position = "dodge") +
  facet_wrap(~ sorted + compartment, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "UMIs per positive cell (capped at 10)", y = "cells (log scale)", fill = NULL,
       title = "How deeply each feature is sampled where it is detected") +
  theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "top")
```

# Agreement with the sort

This is the part worth reading carefully. Using `WPRE-LTR` ≥ 1 UMI as the call:

```{r confusion}
calls <- cells %>%
  dplyr::mutate(called = `WPRE-LTR` > 0)

conf <- calls %>%
  dplyr::group_by(compartment, sorted) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(cells = dplyr::n(),
                   called_pos = sum(called),
                   pct = 100 * mean(called),
                   .groups = "drop")

conf %>%
  dplyr::mutate(pct = round(pct, 2)) %>%
  DT::datatable(rownames = FALSE, options = list(dom = "t", pageLength = 10),
                caption = "Transcript-level calls within each sort fraction")
```

Read down the `wild-type` rows first. Those cells have no vector in their genome at all, so every
positive there is assay error, and the rate is the honest false-positive floor of the measurement.

Now the two surprises:

**Sorted-positive cells are often transcript-negative.** Only part of the `FACS mCherry+` fraction
carries a detectable cassette transcript. These are not sorting errors: the cell was red enough to
pass the gate, so the protein was there. Fluorescent protein accumulates and persists, whereas mRNA
is present in a few copies and sampled shallowly — a cell can be brightly mCherry⁺ while its handful
of transcript molecules are missed entirely. This is dropout, and it sets the ceiling on sensitivity.

**Sorted-negative cells carry transcript well above the wild-type floor.** This is the observation
worth pursuing, and the next section is about what it can and cannot mean.

```{r metrics}
fp_floor <- conf %>%
  dplyr::filter(sorted == "wild-type (no vector)") %>%
  dplyr::summarise(rate = max(pct)) %>% dplyr::pull(rate)

conf %>%
  dplyr::mutate(`fold over wild-type floor` = round(pct / fp_floor, 1),
                pct = round(pct, 2)) %>%
  dplyr::rename(`% called positive` = pct) %>%
  DT::datatable(rownames = FALSE, options = list(dom = "t", pageLength = 10),
                caption = sprintf("Wild-type false-positive floor: %.2f%% of cells", fp_floor))
```

# Why do sorted-negative cells carry transcript?

Four explanations are possible, and the UMI depth distinguishes them.

**Ambient contamination within the tube.** Free transcript from lysed cells is captured in other
droplets. It is tempting to rule this out by pointing at the wild-type tubes, but that reasoning does
not hold: a wild-type tube contains no vector anywhere, so it bounds only the *cross-tube* and
mismapping error. A sorted-negative tube that contains even a few genuinely transduced cells has its
own internal ambient pool, and those cells express the cassette strongly. The wild-type floor
therefore says nothing about how much ambient a vector-containing tube carries. Ambient produces
almost exclusively 1-UMI cells.

**Sort impurity** — gate leakage. Flow sorts are typically 95–99% pure, so a few percent of truly
mCherry⁺ cells in the negative fraction is expected. Leaked cells are ordinary positive cells, so
their UMI distribution should match the positive fraction.

**Transduced but below the protein gate** — an integrated, transcribed cassette whose mCherry never
accumulated enough to sort as red, through promoter silencing or low copy number. These would carry
transcript at levels between ambient and the sorted positives.

**Cre-mediated excision** — the cassette is loxP-flanked, so Cre removes promoter and payload
together. This explains sorted-positive cells lacking transcript, since protein persists after the DNA
is gone, but it cannot create transcript in a negative cell.

The first three predict different depths, so the distribution decides between them:

```{r negative-diagnosis, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 4}
calls %>%
  dplyr::filter(`WPRE-LTR` > 0, sorted %in% c("FACS mCherry+", "FACS mCherry−")) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(umi_capped = pmin(`WPRE-LTR`, 12)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(factor(umi_capped), fill = sorted)) +
  geom_bar(position = "fill") +
  facet_wrap(~ compartment) +
  labs(x = "WPRE-LTR UMIs per positive cell (capped at 12)",
       y = "proportion of cells at this depth", fill = NULL,
       title = "Depth of transcript in positive cells, by sort fraction",
       subtitle = "leaked positives would match the FACS mCherry+ profile; sub-gate expressers sit lower") +
  theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "top")
```

```{r negative-summary}
calls %>%
  dplyr::filter(`WPRE-LTR` > 0) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(compartment, sorted) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(`positive cells` = dplyr::n(),
                   `median UMI` = median(`WPRE-LTR`),
                   `mean UMI` = round(mean(`WPRE-LTR`), 2),
                   `% with ≥2 UMI` = round(100 * mean(`WPRE-LTR` >= 2), 1),
                   `% with ≥5 UMI` = round(100 * mean(`WPRE-LTR` >= 5), 1),
                   .groups = "drop") %>%
  DT::datatable(rownames = FALSE, options = list(dom = "t", pageLength = 10))
```

If the sorted-negative positives were leaked positives, these rows would be indistinguishable. They
are not: in the HSC compartment the sorted-positive fraction has a median of 2 UMIs with 63% of
positive cells at ≥2, while the sorted-negative fraction sits at a median of 1 with only 15% reaching
≥2 and almost none reaching 5. The negative fraction's signal is overwhelmingly single-UMI.

That points at **ambient within the tube** as the dominant source, not a large population of
sub-gate expressers. The cutoff scan below makes the same point more sharply: requiring 2 UMIs
removes most of the sorted-negative signal while retaining most of the positive signal.

This does not mean the sorted-negative fraction is free of transduced cells — a minority tail does
reach higher depth, and those cells are real. It means the headline rate of cells with ≥1 UMI
overstates that population badly, and any analysis treating ≥1 UMI as "transduced" would be mostly
labelling ambient. The sort fractions remain the better genotype assignment; the transcript adds a
way to find the leaked minority within them, not a replacement.

# Where the signal sits on the UMAP

```{r umap, fig.width = 11, fig.height = 4.5}
calls %>%
  dplyr::filter(pass_cell) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(`WPRE-LTR` > 0) %>%
  ggplot(aes(UMAP_1, UMAP_2, colour = `WPRE-LTR` > 0)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.2, alpha = 0.6) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "grey85", `TRUE` = "firebrick"),
                      labels = c("not detected", "WPRE-LTR+")) +
  facet_grid(compartment ~ sorted) +
  labs(colour = NULL, title = "Transgene-positive cells across the QC-passing populations") +
  theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "top")
```

Whether the sorted-negative positives form a coherent region or scatter across the embedding is
informative: leaked positives should sit wherever the positive population sits, while a distinct
location would suggest a particular cell state loses or silences expression.

# Choosing a call

```{r threshold-scan}
scan <- lapply(1:5, function(k) {
  calls %>%
    dplyr::group_by(sorted) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(rate = 100 * mean(`WPRE-LTR` >= k), .groups = "drop") %>%
    dplyr::mutate(cutoff = k)
}) %>% dplyr::bind_rows()

ggplot(scan, aes(cutoff, rate, colour = sorted)) +
  geom_line() + geom_point() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "WPRE-LTR UMI cutoff", y = "cells called positive (%, log scale)", colour = NULL,
       title = "Raising the cutoff trades sensitivity for specificity") +
  theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "top")

scan %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = sorted, values_from = rate) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(-cutoff, ~ round(.x, 3))) %>%
  DT::datatable(rownames = FALSE, options = list(dom = "t"))
```

The wild-type column is the false-positive rate at each cutoff and the `FACS mCherry+` column the
sensitivity, so the table is a small ROC — with the `FACS mCherry−` column showing how much of that
fraction's signal survives.

The step from 1 to 2 UMIs is the one that matters. It costs a modest share of the sorted-positive
cells while removing the great majority of the sorted-negative signal, which is the behaviour
expected if that signal is ambient rather than a population. Going beyond 2 buys little further
specificity and keeps costing sensitivity.

Use `WPRE-LTR` for the call — it is the only feature sensitive enough to threshold — at **≥2 UMIs**
unless the downstream analysis specifically tolerates contamination in exchange for recall.

# Caveats

The three features are **not independent measurements**. They are three windows on one mRNA, so they
must not be summed or averaged as separate genes. `WPRE-LTR` is the measurement; `mCherry` and `DRE`
confirm the sequence is what it should be and, by their ordering, demonstrate the positional effect.

A zero does not mean untransduced. It means no cassette transcript was captured, which covers
untransduced cells, Cre-recombined cells that lost the cassette, silenced cells, and cells whose
transcript was simply missed. Only the wild-type tubes are known to be vector-free.

Counts are from `mpn_raw_processed_*`, before the QC filters are applied — the UMAP panel restricts
to `pass_cell`, but the tables do not, so that the ambient floor is measured on the same unfiltered
population throughout.
